accountability = the duty of those in power to explain and justify their actions
corruption = dishonest use of power for private gain, such as taking bribes
bribery = offering or taking money or gifts to influence an official decision
nepotism = giving jobs or favours to relatives rather than on merit
freedom of information = the right to see official documents held by the state
propaganda = information spread to promote a political cause, often one-sided
prosecute = to bring a criminal case against someone in court
defendant = the person accused of a crime or sued in a civil case
community service = unpaid work for the community, given as a punishment
petty crime = relatively minor offences such as shoplifting or vandalism
organised crime = crime planned and carried out by structured groups
prosecutor = the lawyer who presents the case against the accused
defence lawyer = the lawyer who represents the person accused of a crime
jury = a group of citizens who decide if the accused is guilty
verdict = the decision of a jury or court at the end of a trial
acquit = to formally find that someone is not guilty
convict = to find someone guilty of a crime
life imprisonment = a prison sentence for the rest of a person's life
probation = a sentence served in the community under supervision instead of prison
parole = early release from prison under conditions
